title: Nepal Begins Reconstruction of Heritage Sites
main_content:
Nepal has begun reconstruction of ancient key temples and monuments, including a UNESCO heritage site, that were damaged in a massive earthquake one year ago.

Nepali officials say it will take years to fully restore the South Asian country’s architectural heritage and rebuild 600,000 homes destroyed in the 7.8 magnitude earthquake that upended roads in the country and turned mountain villages into rubble.

International donors have pledged $4.1 billion toward Nepal’s recovery, but only $1.3 billion has been sent to the country, with the government blamed for taking months to set up the National Reconstruction Authority.

In Nepal, protesters chanted “Government, where is [the] reconstruction?” as they tried to force their way into government offices.

“We are hoping that the government’s priorities and perspectives on reconstruction will soon be clear so that we can help people to rebuild and get their lives back on track as quickly as possible,” one Red Cross official in Nepal said.

The Red Cross says four million people are living in shelters.

Homeless survivors have been promised about $2,000 in aid, but only several hundred have received the first $500 installment.

According to reports by VOA’s Tibetan Service, Tibetan villages along Nepal’s border, which were also destroyed by that same quake, have yet to be rebuilt, and many of an estimated 100,000 internally displaced Tibetans remain without homes to return to.

It is not clear whether the construction will focus on rebuilding damaged homes or simply moving displaced Tibetans into new towns, as Beijing has done before.

questions.question: Why is Nepal rebuilding several temples and monuments?
options: To promote tourism after the earthquake disaster
To restore the architectural heritage damaged by the earthquake
To satisfy international donors who have pledged financial aid
To replace modern structures with ancient designs
questions.answer: To restore the architectural heritage damaged by the earthquake

questions.question: What reason do people have to blame the government?
options: For failing to mobilize international support quickly enough
For taking months to set up the National Reconstruction Authority
For not providing adequate food and resources to survivors
For focusing too much on restoring temples rather than homes
questions.answer: For taking months to set up the National Reconstruction Authority

questions.question: How much money will the homeless survivors receive from the government?
options: Up to $2,500 depending on family size
A total of about $2,000 in aid
An initial payment of $1,000 followed by installments
Only $500 with no further payments promised
questions.answer: A total of about $2,000 in aid
